emergent_label: Sanctions Screening and List-Maintenance Program Failures
rationale: The search returned no close match: SAN005 Name Screening Evasion is the closest sanctions-family candidate but that doctrine concerns a LISTED PARTY disguising its name to defeat screening, whereas page 1 states Bank of America had exact name- and date-of-birth matches to blocked persons and the failure was internal -- the bank 'failed to appropriately prioritize alerts' for those exact matches, 'failed to promptly update watchlists following OFAC designations', 'processed payments involving blocked banks', and 'mishandled two business accounts associated with blocked persons due to human error'. This is a bank-side sanctions compliance program failure (alert triage, list-maintenance timeliness, and payment processing controls) rather than an evasion technique used against the bank, so no existing typology fits and this is proposed as emergent.

citations.quote: Bank of America processed payments involving blocked banks
failed to appropriately prioritize alerts for customers who were exact name- and date of birth-matches to blocked persons
failed to promptly update watchlists following OFAC designations
mishandled two business accounts associated with blocked persons due to human error
